exercises.title: Advanced Instrument Use: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: How do you measure ringing on a switch node accurately?
choices: Use a short probe ground spring and a scope and probe bandwidth well above the ringing frequency
Use the long ground lead and turn on the 20 MHz bandwidth limit for a cleaner trace
Use a 1× probe for more signal
Average many captures to remove the ringing
hints: Probe loops and bandwidth limits change what you see.

exercises.title: Advanced Instrument Use: worked analysis
exercises.instructionMarkdown:
Capture converter startup, switch-node ringing, rail ripple, and an intermittent protocol failure without corrupting them.

Show assumptions, equations, units, standard-value choices, ratings, tolerance effects, and the measurements that would verify the result.
checklist: I drew or described the complete source and return path.
I carried units and checked the order of magnitude.
I checked ratings and at least one worst-case condition.
I wrote an observable verification step before viewing the solution.
hints: Start with a symbolic relationship before substituting numbers.
Separate typical behavior from guaranteed limits and add measurement tolerance.
exercises.solutionMarkdown:
## Reference solution

Use a short spring ground or differential probe for switch-node ringing; bandwidth-limit only when measuring rail ripple and state the limit. Degauss and zero the current probe. Use segmented memory or protocol triggers for intermittent traffic, enough record length for low-frequency behavior, and an electronic load with four-wire sensing where lead drop matters.

The governing principle is: **match probe, bandwidth, grounding, sampling, and trigger to the phenomenon being investigated**. Define every reference direction and convert values to coherent SI units. Compare the result with component ratings and standard available values, then report a bounded expectation that includes tolerance, temperature, supply variation, and instrument loading.

### Verification evidence

1. Power off and confirm wiring, polarity, and discharge state.
2. Configure a conservative current limit.
3. Predict source current and the critical node voltages or waveform features.
4. Power on and compare the first measurement with the bounded prediction.
5. Stop if current, temperature, smell, or waveform exceeds the safe bound.

The notebook should make both the reasoning and bench test independently reproducible.

exercises.title: Advanced Instrument Use: measurement and fault investigation
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Plan or perform a low-voltage investigation of **long probe ground, FFT floor misread, current probe not degaussed, insufficient memory depth**. Record a safe setup, predicted healthy evidence, observed evidence, one hypothesis at a time, and the final verification.
checklist: I documented the de-energized inspection and safe current limit.
I recorded expected healthy readings before measuring.
I used one falsifiable hypothesis at a time.
I included final evidence that distinguishes cause from symptom.
hints: Measure the supply current and block boundaries before probing internal details.
Change only one condition between measurements.
